summary: Pass 3. The single pass-2 blocker is fixed by the prescribed mechanism and both of its consequences are unreachable. resetPresenceConsentForNewConnection() (InterRoomController.swift:319) clears activePresenceMonitoringGranted and activePresenceConsentState and is called synchronously at :485 in connect(configuration:completion:) and :678 in connect(withToken:serverURL:configuration:completion:), after the state and double-connect guards so a refused connect cannot void a live session's consent. The ordering constraint is verified in the code, not assumed: handleTokenResponse spans :696-:772 and every activePresence / reset / apply occurrence in the file is at lines 256-370, 485, 518, 577-580, 625-632 or 678 - none between 679 and 772 - so the main-queue hop that would have clobbered the server's answer does not exist. The scheduled branch now calls applyPresenceSettingsFromScheduledMeeting(_:) unconditionally at :518, assigning all eight fields; /meetings/:id/start is structurally incapable of carrying a presence key (scheduling.js:839 is a literal with seven named top-level keys and a ten-key roomSettings object, no spread, and grep -ci presence scheduling.js is 1 - a comment about LiveKit participant presence) and never calls resolvePresenceArming, so the scheduled room's hash carries no presence field either. Consequence (A) is closed because the detector start site (SecureWindowController.m:612) reads granted, whose only writers are recordPresenceConsent (AppDelegate.m:2509 consent screen, :2562 server confirmation) and the reset, and every session is preceded by a connect through one of the two entry points (four call sites: AppDelegate.m:1303, :2127, :2211, :4894; no internal reconnect), so granted can only be true in a session where this candidate answered this session's consent screen, which renders only when armed is true. Consequence (B) is closed on both sides. Plan D0.1 now holds on all four paths. Item 3 (teardown clearing) was correctly declined: -stopPresenceSurfaces is the first statement of -teardownActiveWindows (AppDelegate.m:6747), which is called at :736 inside -enterMode: - the pre-existing comment at :730-735 documents the same hazard for pendingMeetingSettings - and the three presence read sites run later in that same pass, so clearing there would switch the feature off for every session. Design note 2.2 no longer carries the false claim; new 2.2.1 states it was wrong on two counts and enumerates the four connect paths, each row of which I checked against the code, and there is no fifth path. Five regression tests exist and passed in all four of my runs, with the one seam limitation (tokenService is a let at :105 with no injection point) stated twice rather than skipped. Verification I ran: independent full compile into /tmp/pass3-dd gave ** BUILD SUCCEEDED **, exit 0, 0 error: lines, 693 Swift compile actions, 72 warning lines none of which is at a line this change added (my first build against the user's derived data was up to date and compiled nothing, so I re-ran into a scratch path); token-server npm test gave tests 162 / suites 17 / pass 159 / fail 0 / skipped 3, exit 0, the recorded totals exactly; the three presence files with livekit-server --dev up gave tests 82 / pass 82 / fail 0 / skipped 0, so the three otherwise-skipped arming subtests ran for real and are the live flag-off zero-impact proof plus the flag-on proof that pro-hosted, call-type, EU and under-18 rooms each get no presence key; the 13-class targeted client set (198 cases) ran four times, passing three times and failing once with two pre-existing InterRoomControllerTests cases (testDisconnect_clearsRoomCode exceeded its 2 s wait, then its pending asyncAfter block dereferenced the IUO controller that tearDown had nilled and crashed the runner, the crash being attributed to testDoubleConnect) - not this change: the class alone passes, the same 12 classes without the new test file pass, the full set passed 3 of 3 re-runs, and all five new tests passed every time. I did not re-run the full client suite; the recorded 782 passed / 6 failed exceeds the 4-failure baseline by two SecureTools audit tests that enumerate inter/UI/SwiftUI/SecureTools from #filePath, a directory this change never touches, which holds 12 .swift files with none of the forbidden networking tokens, so the failure is the sandboxed runner being unable to enumerate ~/Documents; recommend correcting the recorded baseline to 6 on this machine. Hard constraints intact: greps over both changed client files return nothing for score/rating/risk/percentile/aggregate/index and nothing for emotion/affect/engagement/attention/personality/honesty/confidence/cheat/proctor/gaze/iris/yaw/pitch/roll/blink/landmark/virtual-camera/room-scan (the one hit is promotion/demotion at :1396, pre-existing role vocabulary); no new call site, request or UI affordance, so no automated action; the ingest forbidden-key 400 is untouched and green with 16 assertion sites naming PRESENCE_FORBIDDEN_FIELD plus the live assertion at presenceGate.test.js:576; multipleFacesEnabled() is still a strict === 'true' with the false-positive-study prerequisite at presenceConfig.js:55-59; flag-off zero impact is preserved because the reset writes values the properties already hold and no KVO observer is registered on any activePresence key (only connectionState, participantPresenceState, activeSpeakerIdentity and remoteParticipantCount are observed, InterMediaWiringController.m:1042-1051). REMOVAL.md matches the tree: I re-measured its three marker greps myself at 38 / 37 / 15, all 22 listed files exist, and the seven InterRoomController.swift anchors match. No merge blockers remain. Seven production prerequisites stay outstanding and are recorded below. livekit-server --dev was started and stopped (no listener on 7880); no token server was started; no database row was created and no migration run; no git command was run and no production code was modified.

blockers_before_production.detail: No published candidate-facing transparency page. The consent copy points at a page that does not exist yet. Recorded in design note section 10. Deliberately deferred by the user; blocks enabling PRESENCE_MONITORING_ENABLED for real candidates, not merge.

No candidate copy/delete (DSAR) endpoint. PRESENCE_RIGHTS_CONTACT is an email address, not a mechanism: retention and the purge sweeper are built, subject access is not. Recorded in design note section 10. Deferred by the user; blocks enabling the flag for real candidates, not merge.

The multiple_faces false-positive study has not been run: at least 20 sessions across varied lighting, rooms, webcams and skin tones, per-session false-positive rate under 5 percent for that event type. Prerequisite documented at presenceConfig.js:55-59 and design note section 7.1, and the signal is default-OFF behind a strict === 'true' until it passes. This study is also the keep-or-delete decision for the whole feature.

No resource and battery measurement of the on-device detector under a real interview load. Recorded in design note section 10. Deferred by the user; blocks enabling the flag for real candidates, not merge.

Legal review of the four named questions in design note section 3.4 is outstanding, including the EU AI Act Article 5(1)(f) posture this product carries as provider in a hiring context. EU-resident and under-18 candidates are already forced off server-side by resolvePresenceArming, so the shipped default is safe, but the review must land before any rollout.
Threshold ownership is still open: design note section 13 names no owner for the section 6.1 threshold values. Deferred by the user; recorded, not a merge blocker.

observations_not_blockers.detail: Pre-existing flaky test, out of scope for this change. testDisconnect_clearsRoomCode (:90-:104) schedules a DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter(+0.5 s) block that dereferences self.controller but waits only 2 s; controller is an implicitly-unwrapped optional (:8) that tearDown nils (:15), so when the deadline is missed under parallel-worker CPU contention the test fails on the wait, tearDown nils the controller, and the pending block then dereferences nil and crashes the runner, with the crash attributed to whichever case was executing (here testDoubleConnect_whenAlreadyConnecting_returnsError). Observed once in four runs of the 13-class targeted set; reproduced zero times in three further runs, and the class alone and the same 12 classes without the new test file both pass.

Recorded-baseline correction, not a finding. The full client suite's 6 failures exceed the recorded 4-failure baseline by SecureToolsNetworkAuditTests.testSecureToolsSourcesImportNoNetworkingModules and SecureToolsWindowAuditTests.testSecureToolsSourcesContainNoWindowSpawningAPIs. Both resolve inter/UI/SwiftUI/SecureTools from #filePath and FileManager.enumerator it; that directory holds 12 .swift files on disk and a grep over them for 13 of the 16 forbidden networking tokens returns no file, so the property they protect holds and the failure is the sandboxed test runner being unable to enumerate ~/Documents. Neither test reads any file this change touched. Recommend recording the baseline as 6 on this machine, or granting the test runner Documents access.

Prose accuracy, behaviour is in the safe direction. The doc comment on testScheduledMeetingResponse_carriesAnArmedServerAnswer and fix-notes-pass3.md section 5 both say the scheduled assignment is the server's answer 'so if that endpoint ever starts arming rooms the client follows it'. applyPresenceSettingsFromScheduledMeeting does read response.presenceMonitoringArmed, but startScheduledMeeting (InterTokenService.swift:2564) never parses that key from JSON - only createRoom (:1049) and joinRoom (:1184) do - so a future server arming on that endpoint would still arrive as false until the parser is extended. The design note's own section 2.2.1 row states it correctly.

Residual noted in pass 2 section 7 and still present, not reachable harm. The /room/create branch's assignment sits inside 'if ... error == nil' (:571-:580), so a failed create leaves the previous room's armed value; and the branch assigns only three of the eight fields, leaving retentionDays, multipleFacesEnabled, detectorVersion, thresholds and rightsContact from a previous room. On the error path handleTokenResponse returns before the consent gate and no session is entered, every path that does enter a session assigns armed first, and the five informational fields are rendered only to a candidate while the creating interviewer is not the candidate and any path that makes this client a candidate assigns all eight.
